ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Robert Falcon Scott Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient pre-expedition medical assessment before a long Antarctic expedition: history, examination, ECG, blood tests, mental health and alcohol screening, an elevated blood pressure, tobacco counseling, and a wilderness and expedition medicine referral. Concerns: He wants nothing found that would keep him from leading the sledge journeys himself; He remembers scurvy and weeks of exhaustion after his last long sledge journey and wants the expedition's food and medical plan to prevent it. [S]

tr.td: Varenicline 1 mg tablet, one tablet by mouth twice a day after a one-week starter titration (0.5 mg once daily for 3 days, then twice daily for 4 days)
Losartan 50 mg tablet, one tablet by mouth daily; stop during vomiting, diarrhea or dehydration and restart when eating and drinking normally
Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) 250 mg tablet, one tablet by mouth daily whenever no fresh food is available, packed in every sledging ration
once daily when no fresh food is available

tr.td: New patient pre-expedition medical assessment before a long Antarctic expedition: history, examination, ECG, blood tests, mental health and alcohol screening, an elevated blood pressure, tobacco counseling, and a wilderness and expedition medicine referral
Two-week follow-up with home blood pressure readings, and wilderness and expedition medicine consultation
Six-week review: blood pressure on lifestyle measures, tobacco, urine albumin, dental and hearing results
Three-month review: blood pressure above target, starting losartan, and cold-injury and first aid training
Pre-departure review: electrolytes on losartan, blood pressure, mental health, and the expedition medical plan
Same-day sick visit for vomiting and diarrhea

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Wilderness and expedition medicine consultation in two weeks to assess fitness for a long polar expedition and to plan nutrition, cold-injury and altitude precautions, mental health support, and evacuation

Confirm the blood pressure with a validated upper-arm home monitor, two readings morning and evening for seven days, and start lifestyle measures: less salt, more fruit and vegetables, regular endurance training, and alcohol within limits

Stop pipe tobacco: varenicline with a quit date in one week, counseling at each visit, and the quitline; nicotine products avoided because nicotine narrows skin blood vessels and adds to frostbite risk
Baseline PHQ-9 and GAD-7 before a long isolated expedition, repeated before departure, with a mental health and sleep support plan
Dental examination and cleaning, pure-tone audiometry, and an eye examination with a spare pair of glasses before departure

Expedition nutrition plan: energy of about 5,000 to 6,500 kcal a day on man-hauling journeys with a high fat share, weight checked weekly, fresh seal meat when available, and vitamin C 250 mg a day from tablets in every sledging ration when no fresh food is available, with a weekly check of gums and legs

Cold injury and altitude plan: frostbite and hypothermia prevention and field treatment training for all sledging parties, rapid rewarming only when refreezing can be prevented, ibuprofen for frostbite, gradual ascent to the polar plateau with acetazolamide in the medical kit, and a written evacuation and satellite communication plan

Start losartan 50 mg daily because the home average stayed above 130/80 mmHg after three months of lifestyle measures, with electrolytes and creatinine in two to four weeks and sick-day rules: stop it during vomiting, diarrhea or dehydration and restart when eating and drinking normally
Home blood pressure average below 130/80 mmHg before departure
Home average 124/78 mmHg on losartan 50 mg
No tobacco from the quit date, confirmed at each visit
No pipe since the quit date a week after intake; varenicline continued for relapse prevention
Complete a wilderness first aid course with frostbite, hypothermia and evacuation practice before departure
Course completed, with rewarming and casualty-packaging practice
A written expedition medical plan covering nutrition and vitamin C, cold injury, altitude, mental health support, medicines and evacuation, agreed before departure
Plan agreed; a copy travels in the expedition medical kit
